chunks: From him, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from al-Abbas ibn Ma'ruf, from Talhah ibn Zayd, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), that he said:

The prayer (salat) is not performed on a single limb of a man, whether it be a foot or a hand or a head, if it is separate; but if the body is present, then pray over it, even if it is missing from the head, the hand, and the foot.
ai.seo_question: Do you pray over a single separated limb like a hand or foot?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Tusi records this ruling to clarify that the integrity of the 'body' (al-badan) is the primary condition for the validity of the funeral prayer, distinguishing between a detached limb and a complete corpse with missing parts. This reflects the Shia juristic consensus that the prayer is tied to the physical presence of the deceased's main form rather than every constituent part, ensuring practical applicability in cases of amputation or partial remains.
